title: APODICTIC: /adjudicate and /reconstruct
alt: Flowchart. Your manuscript and its Argument State are broken into a claim graph of atomic claims, warrants, qualifiers and typed links, each anchored to your text. In /adjudicate you decide every claim and link: approve it, reject it, or revise it in your own words. A revision becomes a new claim that comes back for a decision. Rejections stay excluded, even after later revisions. Only approved claims and links go into the drafting packet. In /reconstruct a fresh, isolated drafter sees only that packet and returns a new draft with a passage map tracing each passage to approved claims. The draft comes back for your review and is never marked cleared.

steps.caption: Start from your manuscript and the Argument State the engine built from it.
The argument is broken into a claim graph: each claim, warrant, qualifier and link is one record, anchored to your text.
In /adjudicate you decide every record yourself. Nothing is approved for you, and there is no approve-the-rest.
Approve it, or revise it in your own words. A revision is a new claim, so it comes back for a fresh decision.
Reject it, and it stays out: later revisions and re-runs cannot quietly bring it back.
Only approved claims and links go into the drafting packet.
In /reconstruct a fresh drafter, with no tools and no view of your manuscript, writes from the packet alone.
You get a new draft and a map tracing each passage to approved claims. It comes back for your review, never marked cleared.
